facts.statement: The only known fossil of Kaprosuchus is a nearly complete skull found in the Upper Cretaceous Echkar Formation of Niger.
facts.quote: It is known from a single nearly complete skull collected from the Upper Cretaceous Echkar Formation of Niger.

facts.statement: The name Kaprosuchus means "boar crocodile" because its unusually large caniniform teeth resemble those of a boar.
facts.quote: The name means "boar crocodile" from the Greek κάπρος, kapros ("boar") and σοῦχος, soukhos ("crocodile") in reference to its unusually large caniniform teeth which resemble those of a boar.

facts.statement: Kaprosuchus lived during the Late Cretaceous period, specifically the Cenomanian age.
facts.quote: fossil_range: Late Cretaceous (Cenomanian),

facts.statement: The known skull of Kaprosuchus is about 507 mm long, with a lower jaw measuring 603 mm.
facts.quote: Kaprosuchus is known from a nearly complete skull about 507 mm in length in which the lower jaw measured 603 mm long.

facts.statement: The estimated total body length of Kaprosuchus ranges from 2.42 to 3.77 meters.
facts.quote: Its total body length is estimated to be around 2.42-3.77 m.

facts.statement: Kaprosuchus has three sets of tusk-like caniniform teeth projecting above and below the skull, with one lower tooth fitting into notches in the upper jaw.
facts.quote: It possesses three sets of tusk-like caniniform teeth that project above and below the skull, one of which in the lower jaw fits into notches in the upper jaw.

facts.statement: Rugose surfaces on the premaxillae suggest that Kaprosuchus had a keratinous shield at the tip of its snout.
facts.quote: The surfaces of the premaxillae are rugose with the edges elevated above the body of the bone, suggesting that a keratinous shield would have been supported by the rugosities at the tip of the snout.

facts.statement: Kaprosuchus was once thought to be a primarily or exclusively terrestrial predator.
facts.quote: Kaprosuchus was once thought to have been a primarily if not exclusively terrestrial predator.

facts.statement: Fused nasal bones in Kaprosuchus are thought to have reinforced the jaws against compression from a powerful bite.
facts.quote: The fused nasal bones are thought to have provided reinforcement for the jaws against compression associated with a powerful bite.

facts.statement: The telescoped, dorsally positioned external nares of Kaprosuchus are seen as protection against impact when ramming prey.
facts.quote: The telescoped, dorsally positioned external nares are seen as protection against impact if the animal rammed prey with its robust snout.

facts.statement: Kaprosuchus is a member of the family Mahajangasuchidae, closely related to Mahajangasuchus insignis.
facts.quote: Kaprosuchus is a member of the family Mahajangasuchidae along with closely related Mahajangasuchus insignis from the Upper Cretaceous of Madagascar.

facts.statement: Further studies show that Mahajangasuchidae form a sister clade to peirosaurids, grouping with uruguaysuchids as an early diverging branch of notosuchians.
facts.quote: However further studies on the relationship of this family have repeatedly found them to form a sister clade to peirosaurids, forming a clade that in turn groups together with uruguaysuchids such as Anatosuchus and Araripesuchus as an early diverging branch of notosuchians.

facts.statement: Some estimates suggest the total length of Kaprosuchus could have reached around 6 meters.
facts.quote: de lo que se estima que el animal entero debió rondar los 6 metros de longitud.

facts.statement: Kaprosuchus possesses three pairs of tusk-like caniniform teeth projecting above and below the skull, with lower teeth fitting into notches in the upper jaw.
facts.quote: Posee tres pares de dientes caniniformes a modo de colmillos que se proyectan sobre y por debajo del cráneo, de los cuales los de la mandíbula encajan en unas muescas en el maxilar.

facts.statement: A unique feature of Kaprosuchus is the presence of large, rugose horns formed from the squamosal and parietal bones projecting backward from the skull.
facts.quote: Otra característica única de Kaprosuchus es la presencia de grandes cuernos rugosos formados por los huesos escamosal y parietal que se proyectan hacia atrás en el cráneo.

facts.statement: Rugose surfaces on the premaxillae suggest Kaprosuchus had a keratinous shield supported at the tip of its snout.
facts.quote: Las superficies del premaxilar son rugosas con los bordes elevados sobre el cuerpo del hueso, lo que sugiere que había un escudo queratinoso que se apoyaría en las rugosidades en la punta del hocico.

facts.statement: In Kaprosuchus, the eye sockets open laterally and are angled slightly more forward than upward.
facts.quote: En Kaprosuchus, las órbitas oculares se abren lateralmente y están en un ángulo levemente más dirigido hacia adelante que hacia arriba.

facts.statement: Researchers believe Kaprosuchus was a primarily, if not exclusively, terrestrial predator.
facts.quote: Se piensa que Kaprosuchus era un depredador principalmente terrestre, si no de manera exclusiva.

facts.statement: Evidence for terrestrial behavior includes the lateral and slightly forward position of the eyes, suggesting stereoscopic vision.
facts.quote: La evidencia de este comportamiento incluye la posición lateral y algo hacia delante de los ojos, lo que sugiere una vista estereocópica.

facts.statement: Kaprosuchus possessed enormous canine-like teeth with sharp edges that were relatively straight, unlike the recurved, conical, and striated teeth of aquatic crocodylomorphs.
facts.quote: Los enormes caniniformes tienen bordes afilados y son relativamente rectos, a diferencia de los dientes recurvados, cónicos y con estriaciones de los crocodiliformes acuáticos.

facts.statement: Due to a long retroarticular process, Kaprosuchus's jaws were likely capable of opening rapidly with a large gape to allow opposing canines sufficient space.
facts.quote: Dado que el proceso retroarticular de la mandíbula es largo, es probable que las mandíbulas fueran capaces de abrirse rápidamente con una gran apertura para permitirle a los caniniformes opuestos suficiente espacio.

facts.statement: Fused nasal bones may have reinforced Kaprosuchus's jaws against compressive forces associated with a powerful bite.
facts.quote: Los huesos nasales fusionados pudieron haberle provisto un refuerzo para las mandíbulas contra las fuerzas de compresión asociadas con una mordida poderosa.

facts.statement: Dorsally positioned external nostrles would have protected Kaprosuchus from impacts if it charged prey with its robust snout.
facts.quote: Las narinas exteriores posicionadas dorsalmente serían una protección contra los impactos si el animal cargaba contra una presa con su robusto hocico.

facts.statement: A keratinous shield believed to cover the snout tip may have provided additional protection for Kaprosuchus.
facts.quote: El escudo de queratina que se cree cubría la punta del hocico le pudo proporcionar protección adicional.

facts.statement: Kaprosuchus lived during the Cenomanian stage, from 100.5 to 93.9 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Cenomanian to Cenomanian (100.5 to 93.9 million years ago)

facts.statement: The parent group of Kaprosuchus is the family Mahajangasuchidae.
facts.quote: Parent group: Mahajangasuchidae

facts.statement: Kaprosuchus is classified within the class Reptilia.
facts.quote: Class: Reptilia
